newsitem.title: UK: UK farmers rush to harvest first barley.
newsitem.headline: UK farmers rush to harvest first barley.

text.p: Farmers in the south-west of England are rushing to get the first barley harvested.
"The combines have been working flat out in Dorset, Southern Wiltshire and Hampshire," an expert at the ADAS agricultural advisory service said.

Moisture levels were surprisingly low in some barley harvested, he said. But he expressed concern over low specific weights. Even though the first barley harvested is normally of lower quality than the main harvest, specific weights were worse than they should be, he said.
The speed of early harvesting, so soon after a brief dry spell implied that some barley was almost ready before recent rains.
But there was still quite a bit with green straws, "but if it's hot it'll finish quickly," he said.
The first cuts of wheat were likely to be in some two or three weeks' time, he said. There was a possibility that farmers on very light land would start to harvest some varieties earlier.
The tops of wheat in some areas were already changing colour, he noted.
